evidence_relation: independent outcome-metric tension; not direct contradiction on identical setup

sources.citation: Asprone et al., Comparing Fuzzers on a Level Playing Field with FuzzBench (ICST 2022)
locators: §V Results, efficacy/efficiency and coverage-correlation analyses (PDF pp. 7–8)
sources.claim: Compares FairFuzz among nine fuzzers on 12 real-world systems and 183 real-world bugs with 30 runs per fuzzer/benchmark, 23 hours each. Reports FairFuzz among the lowest for efficacy but most efficient for additional crashes/time to last distinct crash; coverage–bug correlation is weak overall and varies more with the subject under test.

sources.citation: Lemieux and Sen, FairFuzz: Targeting Rare Branches to Rapidly Increase Greybox Fuzz Testing Coverage
sources.claim: Reports increased coverage after 24 hours on some benchmarks and faster high coverage on others; the reported primary outcome is coverage and results are benchmark-dependent.

interpretation: Because studies evaluate different versions, targets, metrics, and setups, do not claim one falsifies the other. The tension motivates equal-budget replication with confirmed deduplicated bugs, coverage, and time-to-bug outcomes reported separately.
